the association between hypercalcaemia of non‐parathyroid origin and skin cancer is still not fully elucidated.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the skin is an endocrine organ.
the skin has a complex neuroendocrine network, which can be activated by a number of factors.
the neuroendocrine system has a major impact on skin function, and that the skin has the ability to respond to and produce neuroendocrine factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
skin is a neuroendocrine target and is regulated by neuroendocrine signals in a PTH‐independent manner.
PTH‐independent hypercalcemia is a common finding in patients with nonmelanoma skin cancers, and it is likely that PTH‐dependent hypercalcemia occurs less frequently.
the skin is an important target for PTH and PTH‐related peptide, and this has been demonstrated by the development of hypercalcaemia in patients who have non‐melanomas of the skin.
